**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/26 (Fri) 04:05  
[USER] User is experiencing an issue with Anki browser shutting down upon opening.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] There could be several reasons why Anki browser is shutting down when opened.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested steps to troubleshoot the issue:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Check if your Anki version is up to date.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Try restarting your computer and then opening Anki again.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Check if any add-ons are causing the problem; disable all add-ons and then open Anki browser.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. Try opening Anki browser in Safe Mode by holding down the shift key while launching Anki.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Check for corrupted files in the Anki profile by deleting the "collection.anki2-journal" file.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. If none of the above steps work, try uninstalling and then reinstalling Anki.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If the issue persists, seek further help from the Anki community or support team.  
[USER] Asked for clarification on what the "collection.anki2-journal" file is.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The "collection.anki2-journal" file is a temporary file used by Anki to store changes to the Anki collection database file ("collection.anki2").  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] It ensures data integrity and prevents data loss in case of unexpected shutdowns or errors.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Changes in the journal file are committed to the main database file when Anki is closed normally.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] If Anki crashes or is forcibly closed, changes in the journal file may not be fully committed, leading to data loss or corruption.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Deleting the "collection.anki2-journal" file is a troubleshooting step, but uncommitted changes will be lost.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended backing up the Anki database before attempting to delete the journal file.
